question.problem: What is ${\int }_{4}^{9}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{4}^{9}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\sqrt{x},$ the lower bound is $a=4$ and the upper bound is $b=9.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{9-4}{n}=\frac{5}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{9}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(4+k\cdot \frac{5}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(4+\frac{5k}{n})\cdot \frac{5}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[\sqrt{4+\frac{5k}{n}}\cdot \frac{5}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
